rationale: C08 provides a close, compact designation formula: “I hereby designate [official or agency] as [specified representative or agency] for [a defined statutory purpose].” The child uses substantially the same one-sentence drafting structure, adapted from the Department of Justice and patent-secrecy statute to the Secretary of the Interior and Virgin Islands expenditures. C12 also uses “I hereby designate” but adds authorization, contingency, and acting-judge machinery. C21 concerns delegation of presidential authority but is less similar in wording and structure.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I hereby designate the Secretary of the Interior as the representative of the President to approve the obligation and expenditure ... of the moneys referred to in the said section 7652 (b) (3).
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I hereby designate the Department of Justice as a defense agency of the United States for the purposes of the said chapter 17 of title 35 of the United States Code.
shared_material.explanation: Both directives consist of a concise presidential designation using the distinctive sequence “I hereby designate [designee] as [defined status]” followed by a narrowly stated statutory purpose.
